dedupe_keys.name: pfas transport and retention during riverbank filtration and in saturated columns

description: Oudega, Thomas James and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The completed one-year study covers four Danube riverbank-filtration sites and related column experiments. Companion descriptions report little concentration reduction between river water and groundwater for the observed compounds, with substance-dependent sorption behaviour in columns. Hydrus sorption-module comparisons show that stronger sorption can require more complex representations. These field and laboratory stages are grouped as one assessment family with exact sample overlap unspecified. Historical comparisons with legal limits are not adopted as current drinking-water safety conclusions. The case supports calibration and assessment of filtration transport models within its observed conditions. Coverage is limited to the stated models, observations and application settings. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; software and companion-data terms are distinguished where separately established. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected; linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
